text: A refactor that's functionally identical can still quietly add gas cost. None of your correctness tests catch that, because the contract still behaves correctly — it's just more expensive.
forge snapshot runs your suite and records every test's gas usage into a committed .gas-snapshot file. For a fuzz test, it records mean and median gas, since cost can vary by input.
Two flags turn that file into an enforceable check. Diff compares current usage against baseline. Check exits with an error the moment any test costs more gas than recorded.
Not every increase is a regression — sometimes you're trading gas for a real feature. You regenerate the snapshot deliberately and commit it, making the cost change visible in the PR diff.
Gas snapshots catch cost regressions on tested paths. Lesson 6 looks at what tested paths actually means — and the real limits of coverage as a metric.
